name: VOD Manager
description: Probes movie/series stream quality and language with ffprobe, keeps one winner per configured tier, and prunes the rest — with optional .strm generation for real multi-version playback in Emby/Jellyfin. Dry-run by default.
author: oxios0x00

fields.label: Dry run (log decisions, don't delete anything)
fields.help_text: ON: probes and decides winners but never deletes anything. Turn OFF once a test batch looks right — pruning is a real delete, only recoverable via Dispatcharr's own next refresh.

fields.label: Qualities to keep (one winner per tier)
fields.help_text: Comma-separated, best first. Keeps one relation per listed tier the title actually has (e.g. one 2160p + one 1080p), never eliminates a title for lacking a tier. If none of the tiers match, falls back to the best quality available.

fields.label: Target languages (ISO 639-2, e.g. fre,eng)
fields.help_text: Comma-separated. Keeps the fewest relations whose audio languages together cover this set.

fields.label: Exclude relations matching none of the target languages
fields.help_text: OFF (default): a tier with no matching language keeps its best-bitrate relation anyway. ON: that tier is dropped entirely — can leave a title with nothing kept if no tier matches.

fields.label: Batch size (movies per click)
fields.help_text: Start small (5-25) to validate before scaling up.

fields.label: Max concurrent probes
fields.help_text: Stay below your provider's connection limit — probing uses a real stream connection.

fields.label: Max probes started per second
fields.help_text: Caps launch rate independently of concurrency.

fields.label: Auto-pause queue if error ratio exceeds
fields.help_text: Pauses the queue once this fraction of a batch fails, instead of hammering a struggling provider.

fields.label: [SERIES]
fields.description: Same probe/select/prune pipeline as Films, per episode. Uses the same quality/language/dry-run/concurrency settings above.

fields.label: Batch size (series per click)
fields.help_text: Smaller than the Films batch size — one series can fan out into dozens of episodes.

fields.label: Episode sampling

options.label: Probe first episode per season, apply to the rest (recommended)
Probe first N episodes per season (see setting below)

fields.help_text: Probing every episode is slow on long shows. 'First only' assumes a season is encoded consistently; 'Probe first N' verifies that assumption before extrapolating, falling back to per-episode probing if a season turns out inconsistent.

fields.label: Episodes to probe per season (if sampling = 'Probe first N')
fields.help_text: Higher = more confidence a season is consistently encoded, at the cost of more probes.

fields.label: [TITLE CLEANUP]
fields.description: Cosmetic only — strips junk prefixes from titles (e.g. 'NF - The Matrix' → 'The Matrix'). Never affects quality/language selection.

fields.label: Tags to strip (one per line)
fields.default:
NF -
TOP -
4K-FR -
AMZ -
FR -
FR .
D+ -
D+  -
UNV -
4K-NF -
PRMT -
4K-AMZ -
4K-D+ -
4K-FR-HDR -
4K-FR-
A+ -
A+
4K-A+ -
4K-MRVL -
DWA -
007 -
K-FR -
AR-SUBS -
4M-AMZ -
4K-
fields.help_text: Literal prefixes, matched case-insensitively at the start of the title. Longest match wins; stacked tags are stripped repeatedly.

fields.label: Run title cleanup automatically with Scan + Process
fields.help_text: OFF (default): only runs from the Clean Titles buttons or its own scheduled action.

fields.label: [.STRM OUTPUT]
fields.description: Dispatcharr's Xtream API always serves whichever relation's M3U account has the highest priority, regardless of category — a plain IPTV client can't select a specific quality tier. Writing .strm files pinned to each exact relation sidesteps that, for media servers (Emby, Jellyfin) that read them from disk. Safe to re-run: unchanged files are untouched, and a pruned/removed relation's file is deleted automatically (only files this plugin tracks — nothing added by hand is touched).

fields.label: Dispatcharr base URL (baked into every .strm)
fields.help_text: Must be reachable from your media server, not just from Dispatcharr — a LAN IP/hostname, not 'localhost'.

fields.label: Library root path (inside this container)
fields.help_text: Mount this same path into your media server so it can see the generated files.

fields.label: Run .strm generation automatically with Scan + Process
fields.help_text: OFF (default): only runs from the Generate buttons or its own scheduled action.

fields.label: [TARGETED RE-PROBE]
fields.description: A relation is only ever probed once and trusted forever — if a provider swaps the file behind a stream_id without changing it (confirmed happening for real), the cached quality can go stale silently. Fixes just the one relation you point at, not the whole catalogue.

fields.label: Stream ID to force re-probe
fields.help_text: Copy from a .strm file's URL (?stream_id=...). Works for both movie and episode relations.

fields.label: [SCHEDULE]
fields.description: Runs on its own cron, independent of Dispatcharr's own refresh. Click 'Apply Schedule' again after changing any other setting.

fields.label: Schedule (5-field cron)
fields.help_text: 'minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week'. Default = every 6 hours.

fields.label: Schedule timezone
fields.help_text: IANA timezone name. Leave empty to use UTC.

fields.label: Scheduled action
fields.help_text: Which action the scheduler runs on each tick.

actions.label: [MOVIES] Scan + Process
actions.description: One click: scan for changed movies, then probe/select/prune the batch.

actions.label: [MOVIES] Scan
actions.description: Enqueue movies whose M3U relations changed since last pass.

actions.label: [MOVIES] Process Batch
actions.description: Probe + select + (unless Dry Run) prune the next queued batch.

actions.label: [MOVIES] Queue Status
actions.description: Pending/in-progress/done/error counts and the last run.

actions.label: [MOVIES] Pause Queue
actions.description: Stop Process Batch until resumed.

actions.label: [MOVIES] Resume Queue
actions.description: Clear a pause (manual or circuit-breaker).

actions.label: [MOVIES] Clean Titles
actions.description: Strip configured junk prefixes from movie titles (uses Dry Run).

actions.label: [MOVIES] Generate .strm Files
actions.description: Write one .strm per kept movie relation (needs the [.STRM OUTPUT] settings).

actions.label: [SERIES] Scan + Process
actions.description: One click: scan for changed series, then probe/select/prune per episode.

actions.label: [SERIES] Scan
actions.description: Enqueue series whose M3U relations changed since last pass.

actions.label: [SERIES] Process Batch
actions.description: Fetch each queued series' episodes if needed, then probe/select/prune.

actions.label: [SERIES] Queue Status
actions.description: Pending/in-progress/done/error counts and the last run, for series.

actions.label: [SERIES] Pause Queue
actions.description: Stop Process Series Batch until resumed. Independent of the Movies pause.

actions.label: [SERIES] Resume Queue
actions.description: Clear a pause (manual or circuit-breaker) on the series queue.

actions.label: [SERIES] Clean Titles
actions.description: Strip configured junk prefixes from series titles (uses Dry Run).

actions.label: [SERIES] Generate .strm Files
actions.description: Write one .strm per kept episode relation (needs the [.STRM OUTPUT] settings).

actions.label: [MAINTENANCE] Catalog Stats
actions.description: Snapshot kept movies/series by quality tier. Also runs automatically after Scan + Process.

actions.label: [MAINTENANCE] Force Re-probe by Stream ID
actions.description: Clears the cached probe for one relation (movie or episode) and re-queues its title, using the Stream ID above. Click Process Batch/Series afterward to actually redo it.

actions.label: [MAINTENANCE] Delete .strm Files
actions.description: Deletes every generated .strm (movies and series) and clears the manifest. Real files, real delete.

confirm.title: Delete every .strm file?
confirm.message: Removes all files under the configured Movies/Series .strm subfolders. Your media server will lose them until the next Generate. This does not touch Dispatcharr's own catalogue.

actions.label: [MAINTENANCE] Reset Plugin State
actions.description: Wipes the probe cache, queues, known relations, run history and catalog stats — starts fresh on the next Scan/Process.

confirm.title: Reset all plugin state?
confirm.message: Clears every probe result and queue this plugin has recorded — the next Process Batch/Series will re-probe everything from scratch. Dispatcharr's own movies/series/relations are untouched.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Apply
actions.description: Register or update the periodic task from the [SCHEDULE] settings.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Remove
actions.description: Unregister the periodic task.

confirm.title: Remove the schedule?
confirm.message: Unregisters the periodic task. You can re-create it any time with Apply Schedule.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Status
actions.description: Whether a schedule is registered and when it last ran.

actions.label: [SCHEDULE] Test Fire Now
actions.description: Runs the scheduled action immediately, bypassing the cron timer.
